option_relations.rationale: Developmental delay is a symptom, not a specific diagnosis that directly relates to Sturge-Weber Syndrome in a primary diagnostic sense. While Sturge-Weber Syndrome can cause developmental delay, the option itself is too broad and not a specific disease entity to be equivalent or a supertype of Sturge-Weber.

RASA1-related disorders (Capillary Malformation-Arteriovenous Malformation Syndrome) is a distinct genetic disorder involving vascular malformations, but it is not Sturge-Weber Syndrome. They are different conditions.

Vascular malformation of the nose is a localized finding, not a systemic syndrome like Sturge-Weber Syndrome, although Sturge-Weber Syndrome involves vascular malformations. It is not equivalent to or a supertype of Sturge-Weber Syndrome.
Concurrent Microcephaly-capillary malformation syndrome (MIC-CAP) and Mowat-Wilson syndrome (MWS) are distinct genetic syndromes and are not related to Sturge-Weber Syndrome.
